No tool/handler behaviour changed (the tests use a FakeClient).

Corrected the avatar settings-payload test (django-tests)

CasdoorAvatarClaimSyncTests.test_settings_payload_exposes_local_upload_separately (added in 0.1.163) asserted image_upload_url == '' for a fresh creator, but ensure_creator always attaches a default profile image, so the local upload URL is legitimately non-empty — that default is exactly the local fallback the SPA uses when the Casdoor avatar fails to load. The implementation is correct; the assertion was wrong. The test now asserts image_upload_url is truthy, contains /media/, and is distinct from the Casdoor avatar_url (the avatar_url / image_url assertions are unchanged).

Verification

  • python3 -m py_compile on the edited modules; python -m unittest discover -s tests in cli/ → 23 passed.
  • Django suite still not runnable locally (host budget); backend-tests.yml is the authority post-push. The two previously-failing jobs are expected green now.

0.1.164 - Recurring events (backend + MCP/CLI), course git-binding data model

Context

This round opens a large owner request spanning event recurrence, activity-UI fixes, a full course↔GitHub binding feature with lazy sync, an app-wide developer menu, and MCP/CLI parity for remote agents. It is delivered in CI-verified increments. This first increment lands the backend data-model foundation that the rest builds on, because the backend has real CI test signal (backend-tests.yml) whereas the Flutter apps do not run locally on this host (see AGENTS.md host budget). The remaining scope is captured in docs/TODO.md under "GitHub course binding & activity UX".

What changed

Recurring planner events (backend)

PlannerEvent gained a recurrence rule stored on the single base row (no per-occurrence materialisation):

  • recurrence_freq — N does-not-repeat (default), W weekly, M monthly, Y yearly.
  • recurrence_interval — every N periods (default 1).
  • recurrence_end_date — inclusive last date the series may occur.
  • recurrence_count — total occurrences including the first.

Migration planner/0004_plannerevent_recurrence.py (additive; the four fields all have defaults / are nullable, so it is safe on the live DB).

calendar_week_payload (notes/services.py) now expands the series into the requested window:

  • New helpers _add_months (day-clamping, leap-safe), _add_period, _expand_occurrence_dates (honours end-date and count, guarded by a 4000-occurrence ceiling), and _occurrence_payload (shifts starts_at/ends_at by the day delta so the time-of-day is preserved and tags occurrence_date).
  • The grid query now selects one-time events inside the window plus every recurring series (its base may predate the window) and expands each. Recurring series contribute their single next upcoming occurrence (400-day horizon) to the deadlines/urgency list so a weekly class does not flood it.

planner_event_payload exposes the four recurrence fields; PlannerEventWriteSerializer accepts them (choice/int/date validation); the list-create and detail-patch views persist them.

Course git-binding data model (foundation only)

Course gained additive git fields (migration courses/0006_course_git_binding.py): git_provider, git_repo (owner/name, empty = unbound), git_branch, git_sync_enabled, git_sync_timeout_minutes (owner-tunable lazy-commit debounce, default 5), git_pending_since, git_last_synced_at, git_last_sync_error. No new model type was introduced, per the owner requirement. Import/bind/unlink endpoints, the lazy-sync worker, effective logging, the repo selector UI, and MCP/CLI course-git tools are tracked in TODO for the next increments.

MCP / CLI parity

create_event and update_event in both backend/mcp/tools.py and cli/notechondria_mcp/tools.py accept the four recurrence params, and _event_payload returns them, so remote agents can create and read recurring events. Schemas document the N/W/M/Y enum and the end-date-OR-count contract.

Verification

  • python3 -m py_compile passed on every edited backend/CLI module (services, models, migrations, api, mcp/tools, cli tools, tests).
  • Added HeatmapApiTests cases: weekly expansion from a pre-window base, recurrence_count cap, and recurrence_end_date bound.
  • Full Django test run and Flutter builds are not run on this host (no local interpreter/toolchain, host-budget rule); backend-tests.yml is the authority once pushed.

Not done this round (see docs/TODO.md)

Course↔GitHub import/bind/unlink + lazy sync worker + effective logs + Cloudflare-style repo selector; Veronica-7 template repo creation; activity-UI fixes (dark-theme event colours, long-press/right-click edit, recurrence dialog, course filter, ICS-import feedback modal); developer menu in planner + portal; experimental-features registry entry; MCP/CLI course-content-over-API-key tools.

0.1.163 - Drag-to-draw events, heatmap auto-fit, Casdoor avatar fallback

Context

Owner list this round: (1) enable drag-and-draw event creation in the horizontal 3-day / 1-week calendar; (2) the portal heatmap does not span the horizontal space and should auto-fit the window on mobile and desktop; (3) the Casdoor avatar is not correctly processed/updated — when Casdoor is offline use the legacy uploaded avatar, when Casdoor is read always use the Casdoor avatar.

What changed

Drag-to-draw event creation (portal, 3-day / 1-week)

The hour-grid create gesture is now a plain vertical drag (was a long-press) that draws the event's real time span — the drawn band's start AND end become the new event's start/end (previously the end was discarded and every event defaulted to one hour). The vertical drag wins the gesture arena over the parent scroll (scroll the grid via wheel / scrollbar / hour-label column); the outer horizontal drag still navigates weeks. A near-zero drag (tap) falls back to a one-hour block. The create dialog gained a start/end time pair; endsAt is plumbed through onCreatePlannerEvent (new named-optional param) into both the cloud and device-local create paths. The backend already forces ends_at > starts_at.

Heatmap auto-fit (portal front page)

_HeatmapSection rendered ~53 weeks of fixed 13 px cells inside a horizontal scroll view, so it overflowed on phones and left wide cards half-empty. It now uses a LayoutBuilder to show the most recent weeks that fit and scales the cell size (9–16 px) so the grid spans the available width in a fixed-height band on both mobile and desktop. No horizontal scroll.

Casdoor avatar: robust claim + offline fallback

Root causes + fixes:

  • Backend claim. CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR defaulted to avatar only — Casdoor's custom token field, present only when the operator enabled it in the application Token Format. Tokens carry the standard OIDC picture claim by default. Default is now avatar,picture (_claim_str takes the first non-empty), so avatars resolve regardless of token-format config.
  • Backend payload. image_url was avatar_url or local — once a Casdoor avatar_url was set, the locally-uploaded image URL was never sent, so the SPA had no fallback when the Casdoor image failed to load. Both the login/exchange payload and the settings serializer now also expose image_upload_url (the local upload, always); image_url stays the effective avatar for backward compatibility.
  • Frontend fallback (portal). The avatar widget (_RemoteMedia / _RemoteAvatar) now takes a fallback URL: it shows the Casdoor avatar_url first and, when that is empty or fails to load (Casdoor offline / 404), falls back to the local image_upload_url, then the initials placeholder. This realizes "Casdoor when readable, legacy uploader when Casdoor is offline." Older payloads without the new fields fall back to image_url.

Editor and planner get the backend fixes immediately (shared); porting the frontend on-error fallback into their avatar widgets is a follow-up (they retain the prior effective-image_url behavior, not a regression).

Verification

  • Backend: py_compile clean on the changed modules; new CasdoorAvatarClaimSyncTests (avatar-vs-picture claim precedence + image_upload_url exposure in the settings payload). Full Django suite runs in backend-tests.yml CI on push (no local containers on this host).
  • Deployed probe (ntc_… key): the reporting account's avatar_url / image_url already resolve to the Casdoor avatar, confirming the sync path; the fix hardens the claim source and the offline fallback.
  • Frontend: not built locally (no Flutter toolchain / no-local- containers rule) — proven by frontend-pages.yml CI on push. Bracket-balance checks pass on every touched Dart file; no new l10n keys (the drag dialog reuses existing keys; heatmap has no strings).
  • What's-New: two portal FeatureUpdate entries (drag-to-draw, heatmap) added per the standing convention.

Environment variables

  • CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR default changed from avatar to avatar,picture. Operators who set it explicitly are unaffected; those relying on the default now also pick up the OIDC picture claim.

0.1.162 - Offline activities, Google-style month view, debug-log order, rotation logging

Context

Owner bug/feature list: (1) offline users cannot create activities, (2) API key rotation failed with (3) no effective log produced, (4) the 1-month calendar range was unusable (30 hour-grid columns) and should read like Google Calendar's month view, (5) the debug log should show the latest entry at the bottom and auto-scroll.

What changed

Offline / signed-out activity creation (portal)

  • New device-local planner-event store (notechondria.portal.local_events, _LocalAppStore.saveEvents, loaded into _AppShellState._localEvents; counted in the StorageUsageCard buckets; wiped by "Clear all local data").
  • _createPlannerEvent without a cloud session now stores the event locally (id: local-<µs>, is_local: true) instead of returning a "sign in first" error, with §1.7 info logging.
  • _loadActivityWeek + both _loadInitialData boot paths build a local calendar payload for guests (_localWeekPayload, mirroring the server calendar_week_payload shape) and splice local events into server payloads for signed-in users (_mergeLocalEventsIntoWeek), so events created while signed out stay visible after sign-in. No automatic upload — cloud sync of local events is a follow-up.
  • _togglePlannerEventCompletion completes/reopens local events in the local store (string local-* ids never hit the PATCH path).
  • The Activity page no longer blocks signed-out users with the full-surface sign-in prompt; the calendar + create FAB always render. (activitySignInPrompt ARB key is now unused; removal deferred to the next gen-l10n round.)

Month calendar = month grid (portal)

_WideWeekCalendar with the 1-month range now renders _MonthCalendarGrid instead of 30 hour-grid columns: weekday header, weeks as rows, each day cell shows the date (today = filled circle, month shown on the 1st) plus up to a few prioritized event chips — open plans first (heaviest difficulty_weight, then earliest start), feed/session entries next, completed last (dimmed + struck through) — with a locale-neutral +N overflow that opens a day dialog listing everything. Tap a chip for details, tap an empty cell to create an event at that date. Zoom controls hide in month mode (no hour rows); swipe/arrow navigation still shifts by the range length. No new l10n keys needed.

API key rotation: diagnosis + effective logging

The deployed backend rotates fine; the reported failure matches an expired Casdoor session — the app renders from local cache so it looks signed in, but this direct server call 401s. Fixes are on the observability side:

  • Portal + editor onRotateApiKey callbacks now log §1.7-shaped entries (Portal.UI/Editor.UI api_key.rotate) on success AND failure — the failure entry names the cause and the "sign in again" remedy — then rethrow so the existing SnackBar still shows.
  • Shared decode() empty-body ≥400 path used to throw a bare Request failed with <status> with no debug snapshot and no §1.7 shape — a fully invisible failure. It now records a snapshot and throws the shaped message.

Debug log: latest at bottom + auto-scroll (all three apps)

The shared debug-log list renders with reverse: true: entries (stored newest-first) now read chronologically with the latest at the bottom, pinned to the newest entry as lines arrive unless the user has scrolled up (chat UX). The in-card terminal already auto-scrolled.

Verification

  • NOT run locally (docs/AGENTS.md no-local-containers + no-Flutter-toolchain rules): flutter analyze / smoke + locale tests / web builds — proven by frontend-pages.yml CI on the next push. Bracket-balance sanity checks pass on every touched Dart file; no new l10n keys were introduced (gen-l10n not needed).
  • Deployed-backend probes: /api/v1/handshake/ serves 0.1.161; unauthenticated + bogus-JWT POST /auth/rotate-api-key/ return §1.7-shaped 401 JSON (confirming the backend side of rotation is healthy).
  • What's-New registry: two portal FeatureUpdate entries added per the standing convention.

No new or changed variables.

0.1.161 - Pages CI split (frontend/docs independent), backend-tests CI, no-local-containers rule

Context

The 0.1.160 push failed the Pages workflow: the mdBook sanity check correctly caught that docs/SUMMARY.md did not list versions/0.1.160.md — and because the docs build lived inside frontend-pages.yml, the failure also blocked the frontend deploy. SUMMARY.md drift fixed

0.1.160 - MCP agent enablement: gateway route fix, task parity, instructions, CLI batch

Context

Owner priorities this round: make the Activity surface (calendar + tasks) work ASAP, then enable AI agents to remote-test the app and create/manage tasks for the user over MCP — with well-defined instructions for every implemented function and a CLI path for batch work. Mid-round the dev host crashed under a full-stack up --build; the resource rules that came out of that are in docs/AGENTS.md ("Host resource budget") and are now a standing constraint.

Bugs found and fixed

1. /mcp/ unreachable through the Docker gateway

deployment/docker/nginx/default.conf proxied only /api/, /admin/, /static/, /media/ and the three app prefixes; Django mounts the MCP server at /mcp/ (no /api/v1 prefix by design), so every MCP call through the gateway 404'd at nginx while the backend served it fine on the internal origin. This is very likely why "is MCP even running?" was unanswerable. Added the /mcp/ location block (same proxy shape as /api/); documented the reverse-proxy requirement in docs/server/mcp.md.

2. MCP-created planner events diverged from app-created ones

backend/mcp/tools.py _create_event/_update_event wrote raw ORM rows, skipping normalize_planner_event_window (the REST create/PATCH contract: bare-date events get a noon one-hour window; event_date snaps to starts_at's day). MCP responses also returned raw nulls where REST returned the normalized window. Both tools now refresh_from_db() + normalize after save. update_event also gained the REST reopen behavior (is_completed: false clears completed_at), which it silently lacked. Regression tests: test_create_event_normalizes_window_like_rest, test_update_event_reopen_clears_completed_at.

3. Misleading tool schemas

create_event.starts_at/ends_at were documented as "ISO time (HH:MM:SS)" but the model fields are DateTimeFields — an agent following the schema would fail. Now documented as full ISO 8601 datetimes everywhere (both servers).

New capabilities

  • seed_agent_user management command (creators): idempotent agent test identity + fresh ntc_ key on stdout (NOTECHONDRIA_API_KEY=... greppable last line). Guarded by DEBUG=True or ALLOW_AGENT_SEED=1. 3 tests.
  • Baseline MCP instructions on initialize in both servers (backend/mcp/instructions.py ≡ cli/notechondria_mcp/instructions.py, byte-identical parity): data model, task/deadline semantics, common workflows, destructive- tool cautions, batch guidance. User skill.md appended under ## User skill.md when present (previously it was the only content).
  • Tool description/schema upgrade (both servers, planner cluster in full): create/update/delete/list event, get_activity_week (now with the app's days ∈ {3,7,30} range selector), calendar feeds (secret-iCal-URL gotcha), plus PERMANENT warnings on empty_recycle_bin / recoverability note on delete_note.
  • REST planner-events/ GET extras (backward-compatible, opt-in): include_completed=1 and limit= so the CLI can mirror the in-backend list_events exactly. Defaults unchanged.

0.1.153 - "Work offline" escape on the connection-error bar

User report

When the backend is unreachable, the error bar persistently shows "Couldn't reach the server. Check your connection and try again." with only a Retry action — there was no clear way to stop the retries and run the app purely on local storage.

What changed

Added a "Work offline" button to the connection-error bar in all three apps (editor build_helpers.dart, planner + portal app_shell.dart). Tapping it calls the existing _setOfflineMode(true), which:

  • persists offline_mode = true,
  • re-runs _loadInitialData, whose offline branch renders from the local cache and clears the error message (so the bar disappears),
  • and makes every subsequent boot skip remote fetches — the app runs purely on the local-storage module until the user turns the connection back on from Settings → Backend.

The button only shows while offline_mode is off (no point offering it when already offline). The existing Retry + transient dismiss (X) are kept. ARB: +1 key (errorWorkOffline, en/zh).

This pairs with 0.1.150's friendlyError (which produces the localized "Couldn't reach the server" text): network failure now offers a real escape, not just a retry loop.

Verification

  • flutter analyze — 0 errors across shared + all three apps (also confirms _setOfflineMode is reachable from each error bar).
  • flutter test — shared suite + all three smoke tests pass.
  • flutter build web — all three apps pass.

Note (unrelated backend crash)

The reported backend crash was a Postgres connection timeout during migrate (the DB addon was unreachable at deploy time) on the deployed 0.1.150 image — an infrastructure issue, not a code/port change. No new ports were opened by recent work; the backend still exposes only 8000. See the chat for the full diagnosis.

0.1.152 - Version-update notification banner (frontend)

Context

Second half of the version-update feature (handshake-compare approach, owner-confirmed). 0.1.151 added the backend min_frontend_version field; this round adds the frontend banner that consumes it, across all three apps.

What changed

Shared (notechondria_shared)

  • utils/version_status.dart: compareSemver(a, b) (dotted-numeric, pre-release/build suffixes ignored, non-numeric → incomparable), AppVersionStatus { upToDate, updateAvailable, deploying, unsupported }, computeVersionStatus(...), and a BackendVersionInfo carrier.
    • backend version > frontend → updateAvailable (new deploy live, browser still on the cached bundle → refresh)
    • backend version < frontend → deploying (rollout in progress; new bundle served, backend container not flipped yet)
    • frontend < min_frontend_version → unsupported (wins over the version compare)
    • equal / incomparable → upToDate (no banner)
  • components/version_update_banner.dart VersionUpdateBanner: self-contained — owns a periodic probe (default 15 min) + a post-first-frame check, renders a localized top-of-screen banner with a Refresh action (hard browser reload via the web url-strategy), or nothing when current / offline. Soft banners are dismissible; the unsupported one isn't. Returns SizedBox.shrink() otherwise.
  • browserReload() added to the shared web/stub url-strategy.
  • ARB +4 keys (versionUpdateAvailable, versionDeploying, versionUnsupported, versionRefresh).

Per-app wiring (editor / planner / portal)

  • HandshakeResult gained minFrontendVersion, parsed from the handshake min_frontend_version in each verifyHandshake.
  • A _probeBackendVersion() returns BackendVersionInfo? (null when unreachable) by calling verifyHandshake(apiBaseUrl).
  • VersionUpdateBanner(frontendVersion: _kAppVersion, probe: _probeBackendVersion) is hosted at the top of each app's scaffold body (above the error bar).

How it behaves

On boot + every 15 min, each app probes the handshake. If the backend reports a newer version than the running build, the user sees a localized "A new version is available — refresh to update" bar; mid deploy (backend behind the served bundle) shows "rolling out"; a build below MIN_FRONTEND_VERSION shows a non-dismissible "no longer supported — refresh". Offline → nothing (the probe returns null). Designed to also back future mobile update prompts.

Verification

  • version_status_test.dart (semver ordering, incomparable, suffixes; all four status transitions incl. floor precedence).
  • version_update_banner_test.dart (en + zh update banner, refresh button, nothing-when-offline, non-dismissible unsupported).
  • flutter analyze — 0 errors across shared + all three apps.
  • flutter test — shared suite + per-app smoke/locale tests pass.
  • flutter build web — all three apps pass.

0.1.151 - Handshake exposes min_frontend_version (compat floor)

Context

First half of the version-update notification feature (owner picked handshake-compare, no GitHub + add a min_frontend_version floor). This round adds the backend field the frontend will compare against; the frontend banner lands next.

What changed

GET /api/v1/handshake/ now returns a min_frontend_version field — the lowest frontend build the backend still considers compatible. A running client compares its own built version against this floor: below it → a stronger "please update" prompt; at or above → the normal soft "new version available" banner (driven separately by comparing the client version against the live version field, already present).

  • notechondria/api_views.py: new _min_frontend_version() reads the MIN_FRONTEND_VERSION env var (empty string = "no floor", the default), added to the handshake JSON.
  • Env-driven so the floor can be raised at deploy time without a code change.

Verification

  • notechondria/tests.py HandshakeEndpointTests: assert the field is always present (string), and a new test pins the env override (MIN_FRONTEND_VERSION=0.1.140 → reflected; unset → "").
  • manage.py test notechondria.tests.HandshakeEndpointTests — 5 pass.

Environment

  • Optional new env var MIN_FRONTEND_VERSION on the backend. Leave unset (default) for no floor. Set it (e.g. 0.1.140) to force clients older than that to show the update-required prompt once the frontend banner ships.

Follow-up (0.1.152)

Frontend: a shared version-status util + update banner, each app probing the handshake on boot + a periodic poll, comparing _kAppVersion against the backend version / min_frontend_version, with localized "new version available / rolling out / update required" messages and a Refresh action.

0.1.150 - i18n: friendly, localized UI-level error warnings

User request

Add translations for UI-level warnings (not the debug window) — e.g. "client failed to fetch" and similar raw error strings shown to the user.

Problem

When a request fails, the frontend surfaces the raw stringified exception — most visibly in the main error bar (_errorMessage = errors.first). Offline, that reads ClientException: Failed to fetch, uri=…; a 5xx shows a raw HTTP line. Fine for the debug log, gibberish for users (and untranslated).

What changed

  • New shared helper friendlyError(AppLocalizations l10n, Object? rawError) (notechondria_shared/lib/src/utils/friendly_error.dart, exported from the barrel). It classifies the raw error and returns a clean localized sentence:
    • network unreachable (Failed to fetch / ClientException / SocketException / connection refused-reset-closed / XMLHttpRequest / ERR_*) → errorNetwork
    • timeouts → errorTimeout
    • 5xx-shaped failures → errorServer
    • anything else (typically an already-human backend message like "Title is required") passes through unchanged — we never hide a useful server message behind a generic one. The Exception: prefix is stripped.
  • Wired into the main error bar of all three apps (editor build_helpers.dart, planner + portal app_shell.dart): the bar now shows friendlyError(l10n, _errorMessage!). While there, localized the planner/portal error-bar Retry/Dismiss (the editor's were already done in 0.1.141).

The one gap (belated Phase 1 fix)

The Phase 1 audit (0.1.145) claimed full /api/v1/ coverage, but porting list_note_sessions surfaced a miss: NoteSessionListCreateApiView was POST-only — there was no REST GET to list sessions. Added one to backend/notes/api.py, mirroring the MCP tool: filter by ?note_id=, cap ?limit= (default 50, max 200), newest started_at first, returns a bare list of note_session_payload. Covered by a new notes/tests.py test (test_note_session_list_get: lists all, asserts newest-first ordering, and the note_id filter). Every other tool already had a REST endpoint.

CLI parity (30 tools added → 41 total)

cli/notechondria_mcp/tools.py went from the 11-tool starter subset to all 41 tools, each mapping to /api/v1/ via the requests client with the same Bearer ntc_<key> auth. Added:

  • Profile: update_profile.
  • Notes: get_note_by_uuid, search_notes.
  • Note versions: list_note_versions, snapshot_note, restore_note_version.
  • Attachments: list_attachments, delete_attachment.
  • Recycle bin: list_deleted_notes, restore_deleted_note, empty_recycle_bin.
  • Courses: update_course, delete_course, list_course_notes, reorder_courses, subscribe_course, unsubscribe_course.
  • Activity / heatmap: get_heatmap, get_recent_activity, get_activity, get_activity_week.
  • Planner events: update_event, delete_event.
  • Note sessions: list_note_sessions, create_note_session, end_note_session.
  • Calendar feeds: list_calendar_feeds, create_calendar_feed, update_calendar_feed, delete_calendar_feed.

Notable mapping details:

  • unsubscribe_course → DELETE courses/<id>/subscribe/ (the same view that handles subscribe via POST).
  • empty_recycle_bin → DELETE notes/deleted/empty/.
  • end_note_session: the REST PATCH only sets ended_at when supplied (the in-backend tool stamps "now" server-side), so the CLI defaults ended_at to the current UTC time when the caller omits it.
  • get_activity honors its limit client-side (the REST activity/ endpoint always returns the top 10).

0.1.142 - Share-link deep-link fix + i18n Phase 1d (note viewer/editor menus)

User request

Two things: (1) the share URL still doesn't work — https://trance-0.github.io/Notechondria/editor/#/notes/<uuid> lands on the editor home instead of the note preview; (2) continue translation, including the sub-menus.

Share-link deep-link fix

Symptom: a cold-opened share link drops you on the editor home with no note dialog (and not even the private-note prompt) — meaning the fragment was parsed as null.

Root cause: the editor uses Flutter's default hash URL strategy (no usePathUrlStrategy()), and the app is a MaterialApp(home:) with no /notes/<uuid> route table. On the first frame Flutter's router normalizes the unmatched initial route and rewrites the hash from #/notes/<uuid> back to #/. The deep-link read (_parseNoteUuidFromUrl → Uri.base.fragment) runs in _bootstrapApp only after await _loadInitialData() (several seconds), by which point the fragment is already gone. The well-tested parseNoteUuidFromFragment regex was never the problem — the fragment was empty by the time it was called.

Fix: snapshot the launch fragment in main() into the top-level bootInitialFragment before runApp(), while the URL is still pristine. _parseNoteUuidFromUrl() now reads that snapshot first and only falls back to the (possibly-clobbered) live Uri.base. After the note opens, _replaceNoteUrl(uuid) restores #/notes/<uuid> in the address bar as before.

Regression test: editor_app/test/deep_link_open_test.dart — the flutter_test environment has an empty Uri.base.fragment (exactly the clobbered production state), so the test only passes if the boot snapshot drives the deep link. It seeds bootInitialFragment = '/notes/<uuid>', boots with a fake client, and asserts the note viewer opens on the shared note. The existing deep_link_parser_test.dart still covers the pure regex.

i18n Phase 1d — note viewer/editor sub-menus (en + zh)

  • Note viewer (components/note_viewer.dart) — the share-link preview page itself: Back, Untitled note, Options, and the options menu (Edit / Copy link / Export markdown / Delete) + the "Link copied" snackbar.
  • Note editor (modules/note_editor.dart) — the "More actions" menu (Edit note meta, Switch editor: Plain text / Live markdown, View attachments), the Copy-link button + snackbar, and the Title / "Write your note…" / Attach-file hints.
  • Private-note / load-error dialogs (core/auth_flows.dart) — the "Private note" prompt (title, body with the deep-link, Close, Open settings) and the private/load error messages.
  • ARB: +~20 keys (note*, privateNote*, plus the {link} / {reason} placeholders). Regenerated AppLocalizations.

Verification

  • flutter test — shared suite + all three apps' tests, incl. the new deep_link_open_test and the parser/locale tests.
  • flutter build web — all three apps pass.

0.1.141 - i18n Phase 1c: navigation + home feed translated

User request

The language switch still "did nothing" — the setting saved but the UI stayed English, and "no effective debug string was produced". Continue translation and fix the UI text errors.

Diagnosis

The switch mechanism is not broken. A reproduction test (test/locale_switch_test.dart) boots the editor with locale: zh already persisted and confirms the live MaterialApp resolves the zh locale (Localizations.localeOf == zh) and renders Chinese widgets. The whole chain is sound: picker → _setLocale → _applyLocalAppSettings → onLocaleChanged → _handleLocaleChanged → setState → MaterialApp.locale. The same onLocaleChanged runs at startup (load_local_state), so a saved locale is applied on boot too.

The real problem was coverage: 0.1.140 only translated deep settings strings, so flipping the language left the entire high-traffic UI — the navigation and the notes feed a user stares at every session — in English. It looked like nothing happened.

  • The create-category and edit/subscribed-category dialogs: titles, "Category name" field, "Icon:" label, Change/Choose, the delete & subscribed help text, and every action button (Cancel/Create/ Delete/Unsubscribe/Save).

Home / notes feed (modules/learner.dart)

0.1.139 - splash particle density scales with screen size

The view already calls setSize with the widget constraints, so the field auto-rescales when the window resizes.

Calibration points: 1920×1080 → 128; 960×1080 → ~64; a 360×640 phone clamps up to 24 (not left empty); an 8K monitor caps at 320 (not overwhelming).

Highlights:

  • Why: the in-backend /mcp/ tools call the Django ORM directly (backend/mcp/tools.py), so MCP can only run where the full backend runs — no distributable/self-hosted story, coupled release cadence, and doc drift.

  • 5 phases: API gap audit → CLI skeleton → full tool parity → distribute (PyPI) → cutover + delete backend/mcp/.
  • Records open questions for the owner (separate repo vs cli/, Python vs TypeScript, keep /mcp/ hosted or fully cut over) and flags the stale auth-header example in docs/server/mcp.md to fix in Phase 1.

0.1.134 - planner Activity view works offline (no sign-in required)

User request

The Activity view was sign-in only; fix it so it loads cached/local data from the browser like the rest of the app.

Root cause

In planner_app/lib/core/initial_data.dart, the signed-out branch of _loadInitialData blanked the planner state it had just loaded from the local cache at boot:

} else {
  plannerEvents = const [];
  activityWeek = null;   // <- wiped the cached/seeded activity board
  ...
}

plannerEvents and activityWeek are seeded on first run (local_starter.dart) and persisted in the local cache, but this branch overwrote them with empty/null whenever no token was present — so the Activity board showed only the "sign in to view…" empty state. The interactive week navigator (_loadActivityWeek) also early-returned when signed out, leaving the board blank when paging weeks.

What changed

frontend/planner_app/lib/core/initial_data.dart — the signed-out branch now KEEPS the locally-loaded plannerEvents and rebuilds the activity board from them with _buildOfflineActivityWeek() (the same offline builder the first-run seed uses), instead of blanking. Cloud- only data (calendar feeds, server recycle bin, cloud notes) has no local equivalent and is still cleared.

frontend/planner_app/lib/core/settings_actions.dart — _loadActivityWeek now, when signed out, sets the requested week start and rebuilds the offline board instead of returning early, so paging weeks works offline.

Net effect: the Activity view renders the user's local/seeded planner events offline and signed-out, matching how courses already render from cache.

Verification

  • flutter analyze — 0 errors in planner_app.
  • flutter test test/smoke_test.dart passes.
  • flutter build web --release --base-href /Notechondria/planner/ --no-web-resources-cdn passes.
  • No backend changes.

0.1.133 - i18n Phase 1: infrastructure + editor language switcher

User request

Begin implementing the i18n plan (development/i18n_plan.md), editor app first: a Language setting, system-language default, and English (US) + Chinese (Simplified).

What changed

This is Phase 1 of the phased rollout — the localization pipeline plus a working language switcher in the editor app. Planner and portal are untouched (still English) and continue to build against the shared package; their string translation is Phase 2/3.

Shared package — the localization catalog

  • notechondria_shared now hosts the single ARB catalog and generated AppLocalizations consumed by all apps:
    • l10n.yaml (output-dir: lib/src/l10n, real generated Dart — not the synthetic package, so it is importable across packages),
    • lib/l10n/app_en.arb (template) + lib/l10n/app_zh.arb,
    • generated lib/src/l10n/app_localizations*.dart (committed so apps build without a generation step; re-run flutter gen-l10n in the shared package when ARBs change),
    • deps flutter_localizations (SDK) + intl, flutter: generate: true.
  • New lib/src/utils/locale_options.dart: kLocaleOptions (System default / English / 简体中文) and resolveLocale(stored) mapping app_settings['locale'] (system | en | zh) to a Locale? (null follows the device).
  • Barrel exports AppLocalizations, kLocaleOptions, LocaleOption, resolveLocale.

Editor app — language switcher

  • pubspec.yaml: flutter_localizations + intl.
  • MaterialApp (app_shell.dart): localizationsDelegates: AppLocalizations.localizationsDelegates, supportedLocales, and locale: _locale. _locale is driven by a new onLocaleChanged callback that mirrors the existing onThemeChanged plumbing exactly.
  • Locale persistence mirrors theme_preset: locale: 'system' in defaultSettings(), included in _currentAppSettingsPayload, and applied + persisted immediately through _applyLocalAppSettings (which now fires onLocaleChanged). Boot paths (load_local_state, initial_data) push the saved locale on first paint, so the system-language default works for free (a system value leaves MaterialApp.locale null → device locale clamped to the supported set).
  • A Language row in the Editor settings subpage (next to the theme pickers), wired to a new onSetLocale callback that calls _setLocale (the offline-mode-style immediate-apply path). The row's label and the "System default" option are localized via AppLocalizations, so switching to Chinese flips them live (Language → 语言, System default → 跟随系统) — a visible end-to-end proof of the pipeline.

Scope note

Phase 1 deliberately translates only a small demonstrative string set (the Language row + the supported-locale autonyms). The ~130 remaining editor strings, the shared-widget strings, and planner/portal are translated in later phases per the plan — they keep working in English via the template fallback. Planner/portal MaterialApps are not yet wired for a Language setting (Phase 2/3); they follow the device locale for Flutter's built-in widgets only once wired.

0.1.131 - remove legacy "Inbox" categories (duplicate-Inbox bug)

User request

Fix the existing backend database: remove every category named "Inbox" that some historical versions auto-created. The "Inbox" the user sees should only ever be the synthetic uncategorized bucket (notes with course_id IS NULL, labelled by Creator.uncategorized_folder_name, default "Inbox") — never a real Course row. Fix the bug where in some cases an Inbox is auto-created or shows in the UI alongside the default one (a real "Inbox" category and the synthetic bucket rendering at the same time).

Root cause

Pre-0.1.120 builds created a real Course row titled "Inbox" (carrying the now-removed is_default=True) per account. 0.1.120 retired that concept — the uncategorized bucket became a purely client-side render of course_id IS NULL notes — but legacy "Inbox" Course rows linger in older databases, and the editor sidebar renders such a row as a second "Inbox" next to the synthetic bucket. No current code path creates an Inbox Course (the 0.1.101 seed_welcome_note makes a Note with course_id=None, not a course; the local starter stopped creating one in 0.1.120). The 0.1.125 migration prompt let users dismiss it and keep the duplicate indefinitely — that is why the bug persisted.

What changed

Backend — data cleanup command

  • New backend/courses/management/commands/cleanup_inbox_courses.py: deletes every Course whose title is "Inbox" (case-insensitive) and that belongs to a creator (creator_id IS NOT NULL — never touches ownerless/public-catalog rows). Notes are re-parented to course_id = NULL first (explicit UPDATE for an exact moved-count; Note.course_id is on_delete=SET_NULL so nothing is ever lost), then the courses are deleted. Idempotent; --dry-run and --limit N flags; per-course heartbeat.
  • Runbook added at docs/operations/inbox_cleanup.md.

Frontend (editor) — silent auto-migration

  • editor_app/lib/core/inbox_migration.dart: replaced the dismissable once-per-session prompt with silent auto-migration (_autoMigrateLegacyInbox). When a signed-in session loads with an owned "Inbox" category, its notes are reparented to the uncategorized bucket (cloud: deleteCourse → backend SET_NULL; local: drop course_id from drafts and remove the local course) and the category is deleted, surfaced as a SnackBar. Removed the now-dead remove-vs-rename dialog, the _InboxMigrationDecision class, and the moveToCategory branch; _runInboxMigration collapsed to _mergeInboxIntoUncategorized. Runs once per session and self-heals on the next boot if a pass failed offline.

Verification

  • Backend: new courses/tests.py::CleanupInboxCoursesCommandTests (delete + reparent, case-insensitive match, --dry-run no-op, idempotent, ignores ownerless rows, --limit) — 6/6 pass. Full manage.py test suite passes under settings_test.
  • Frontend: editor flutter analyze 0 errors; test/smoke_test.dart passes; flutter build web --release --base-href /Notechondria/editor/ --no-web-resources-cdn passes.

Operator action required

Run the cleanup command once against the live database to remove the legacy rows from existing accounts:

python manage.py cleanup_inbox_courses --dry-run   # audit first
python manage.py cleanup_inbox_courses             # apply

The frontend auto-migration also cleans a signed-in user's own legacy Inbox on next load, but the command is the authoritative sweep.

0.1.130 - first-run onboarding tour

User request

Continue working on tutorials. The remaining Tutorials TODO item was a first-run guided tour, previously deferred because anchored coach marks would need authoring twice around the 960 px drawer/sidebar breakpoint and would break on UI refactors.

What changed

Implemented the first-run tour as a layout-agnostic paged intro instead of anchored coach marks — concept cards (icon + title + body) that never point at a specific on-screen widget, so the same content renders identically on the mobile drawer layout and the desktop sidebar layout. This delivers the onboarding the owner originally asked for while sidestepping the fragility that caused the deferral.

Shared widget

  • New notechondria_shared/lib/src/components/onboarding_tour.dart: TourStep (icon/title/body) and showOnboardingTour(context, appTitle, steps) — a blur-backed, skippable, swipeable PageView dialog with a page-dot indicator, Back/Next, Skip→Close on the last page, and Done. Exported from the package barrel.

Per-app onboarding

  • New lib/core/onboarding.dart part in each app with an app-specific _kOnboardingSteps registry (editor: notes/categories/sync/settings; planner: courses/deadlines/offline/settings; portal: hub/explore/ launch) and an _AppShellOnboardingX extension exposing _maybeShowOnboarding() (first-run, tracked by an onboarding_seen local-stats flag) and _replayOnboarding() (Settings entry point).
  • Wired post-boot in each initial_data.dart: on a brand-new user's first boot the tour shows and suppresses the What's-New / install nudges that boot (if (!_maybeShowOnboarding()) { whatsNew; installBanner; }) so a new user meets one overlay, not three. Returning users (flag set) get the existing nudges as before.

Replay entry point (all three apps)

  • Added an optional onReplayTour callback:
    • editor + portal: a "View tutorial" row in the Settings menu card (plumbed through each _SettingsPage + host build site);
    • planner: a "View tutorial" row in the shared AppPreferencesCard (new optional onReplayTour param), wired from planner's _SettingsPage.

Tests

  • New onboarding_tour_test.dart: opens on step one, advances with Next, Next→Done + Skip→Close on the last step, Done/Skip close the tour, and empty steps render nothing.

Verification

  • flutter analyze — 0 errors across notechondria_shared and all three apps (pre-existing warning backlog unchanged).
  • flutter test — shared suite passes (incl. the 4 new tour tests); all three apps' test/smoke_test.dart pass with the tour now firing on the first-boot smoke scenario (the underlying starter content stays findable behind the modal).
  • flutter build web --release --base-href /Notechondria/<app>/ --no-web-resources-cdn passes for all three apps.
  • No backend changes this round.

Notes for the owner

  • The tour is intentionally not anchored to UI elements, so it will not drift when screens are refactored and needs no per-breakpoint authoring. Edit the step copy in each app's lib/core/onboarding.dart.
  • A returning user who already has local data will not see the tour (the onboarding_seen flag is only unset on a truly fresh install or after a full local-data clear); they can replay it any time from Settings → "View tutorial".

0.1.127 - storage namespacing fix, Casdoor password sync, What's-New overlay, mobile web shell

User request

Implement the three owner decisions from the 0.1.126 cross-platform survey, then continue down docs/TODO.md:

  1. Re-enable the Pages service worker with an in-app "new version available — reload" toast.
  2. Replace the course-based tutorial proposal with a UI overlay that introduces missed features on app version updates, tracked per user (last seen version on the profile) with a skip option.
  3. Keep the email/password Casdoor-outage fallback permanently and auto-sync the Casdoor password into the app database on Casdoor login (Casdoor app config: JWT-Custom, RS256, token fields Password / Password salt / Password type; test account provided).

What changed

Backend — Casdoor password sync (fallback login stays correct)

  • New backend/creators/casdoor_password.py:
    • sync_password_from_claims mirrors the JWT-Custom credential claims (password / passwordSalt / passwordType) into User.password — plain via set_password, bcrypt stored as bcrypt$<hash> for Django's BCryptPasswordHasher. Verified live against auth.trance-0.com: current Casdoor scrubs the password claim value (empty string; passwordType = bcrypt), so this path is dormant until the IdP emits the hash. Tracked in docs/TODO.md (watch upstream).
    • password_grant runs Casdoor's ROPC grant (/api/login/oauth/access_token, grant_type=password) and verifies the returned JWT, distinguishing rejected (Casdoor answered no) from unreachable (timeout / 5xx — the outage case). Live-verified with the Alice test account: correct credentials → ok + verified sub; wrong credentials → rejected.
  • LoginSerializer (backend/creators/api.py): when the submitted password fails the local hash, the backend asks Casdoor via password_grant (with one username-variant retry); on success and a sub match against Creator.casdoor_sub, the verified plaintext is stored locally via set_password and login succeeds. Outcome: the current Casdoor password always works on the fallback endpoint while Casdoor is up, and the locally synced hash serves outages. Unlinked legacy accounts never trigger the grant (no auto-bind, consistent with the 0.1.118 link-challenge policy).
  • _sync_creator_from_claims (casdoor_auth.py) additionally calls the claims-based password sync on its existing 5-minute throttle.
  • settings.py: explicit PASSWORD_HASHERS (Django defaults minus Argon2, plus BCryptPasswordHasher), CASDOOR_CLAIM_PASSWORD* claim-name mappings. bcrypt>=4,<5 added to requirements.txt and requirements-render.txt. settings_test.py gained BCryptPasswordHasher so the sync path is testable.

Backend — per-app What's-New tracking

  • Creator.last_seen_versions (JSONField, migration creators/0035): map of app id → newest version whose feature overlay the user has seen or skipped.
  • Exposed in auth_payload and the settings GET; PATCH /api/v1/settings/ merges keys (editor stamping editor cannot erase planner's entry) and validates shape/size.

Frontend — What's-New overlay (owner's tutorial design)

  • Shared notechondria_shared: FeatureUpdate, compareAppVersions, selectMissedUpdates, showWhatsNewOverlay (blur dialog, feature cards, Skip + Got it — both stamp the current version).
  • Each app: lib/core/whats_new.dart part file with a per-app feature registry and _maybeShowWhatsNew, hooked at the end of _loadInitialData. Last-seen resolution: max(local stats, signed-in profile map); fresh installs stamp silently instead of replaying history. Standing convention: rounds that ship a user-visible feature append a registry entry in the same commit.

Frontend — urgent storage-collision fix (multi-app auth corruption)

  • Root cause from 0.1.126 fixed: _LocalAppStore keys are now per-app (notechondria.editor.* / .planner.* / .portal.*), with a one-time copy-style _migrateLegacyKeys for the old unprefixed values (copy, not move — each app migrates independently; legacy keys left behind for a later cleanup action). Editor's session blob included.
  • Shared OAuth handoff keys (oauth_redirect_uri / oauth_invitation_code / oauth_intent) are now prefixed with the launching app's namespace (derived from logAppTag), with a legacy-read fallback for flows in flight across the deploy.

Web shell — mobile fixes + service worker

  • All three web/index.html: added the missing viewport meta (width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover — iPhone Safari previously rendered the desktop breakpoint on a ~980 px virtual viewport), real titles/descriptions, per-app apple-mobile-web-app-title, and a service-worker update toast (plain JS; offers a one-tap reload when a new build's worker installs behind a controlled page).
  • All three web/manifest.json: real name / short_name / description, orientation: any. Icons remain stock Flutter — tracked in docs/TODO.md.
  • .github/workflows/frontend-pages.yml: the unconditional service-worker strip is now a kill switch — workers ship enabled (web apps can launch offline; Safari bookmark / home-screen usage survives airplane mode after first load); setting the repository variable STRIP_SERVICE_WORKER=true restores the pre-0.1.127 always-network behavior.

Tests

  • Backend: CasdoorPasswordClaimsSyncTests, LoginCasdoorRopcSyncTests (ROPC mocked; sub-mismatch, outage, unlinked-account cases), LastSeenVersionsTests (merge + validation). Updated three stale CasdoorAuthTests cases that still asserted pre-0.1.109/0.1.118 behavior (email auto-link, auto-provision, raw authorize signin URL) and had been failing on unmodified main (verified via a HEAD worktree); they now assert the link-challenge contract, plus a new fast-path-by-sub test.
  • Shared frontend: whats_new_overlay_test.dart for version compare and missed-update selection.
  • Repaired the pre-existing notes.tests.NoteAttachmentByUuidApiTests breakage (14 failures on unmodified main, verified via a HEAD worktree): the class still authenticated with client.login() session auth, which left the DRF chain during the Casdoor cutover. Converted to DRF token credentials, updated the anonymous expectation to 401, made the two non-owner tests use a public note so they reach the intended 403 owner guard (a private note 400s at the UUID access check first), and matched the storage-path assertion to the actual dashless uuid.hex path segment.
  • Planner + portal pubspec.lock refreshed (flutter pub get) so their web builds resolve the shared package's idb_shim transitive dependency — same fix 0.1.123 applied to the editor only; both web builds failed before this.

Verification

  • Backend: full manage.py test under DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=notechondria.settings_test in a local Python 3.12 venv pinned to Django 4.2.10 (backend/.venv). creators suite: 46/46 pass; full-suite result recorded in docs/LLM_CHECK.md round log.
  • Live Casdoor verification against auth.trance-0.com with the Alice test account: ROPC grant ok / rejected paths, RS256 + audience verify, and the empty-password-claim finding. No password material was logged or committed.
  • Frontend: dart format on changed files; flutter analyze — 0 errors in all three apps (pre-existing warning backlog unchanged); flutter test test/smoke_test.dart passes in all three apps; notechondria_shared tests pass (whats_new + existing); flutter build web --release --base-href /Notechondria/<app>/ --no-web-resources-cdn for all three apps with built output spot-checked for the viewport meta, real titles, and service-worker registration.

0.1.126 - cross-platform survey: mobile web gaps, auth-corruption root cause, tutorials plan

User request

Survey documented bugs and unimplemented features, assess mobile/web compatibility (the owner uses the apps via Safari bookmarks on iPhone with no Apple computer available), investigate the "multi app auth is corrupting" symptom, and produce a detailed progress snapshot plus a plan for tutorials integration and cross-platform reliability.

What changed

Documentation-only round; no code changes.

  • Added docs/development/cross_platform_plan.md: progress snapshot at 0.1.125, prioritized mobile-web findings (F1–F7), tutorials-integration design, phased roadmap (A–D), manual cross-platform test matrix, and the open owner decisions.
  • Root cause identified for the multi-app auth corruption (F1): on GitHub Pages all three apps share one browser origin, and web shared_preferences is origin-scoped — editor / planner / portal use identical storage keys (notechondria.local_*, notechondria.session in each app's lib/core/local_store.dart, plus the unprefixed oauth_* handoff keys in notechondria_shared/lib/src/app_shell/app_shell_oauth_mixin.dart:196-198), so the apps overwrite each other's sessions, settings, drafts, and OAuth intent. Native desktop builds are unaffected, which is why the symptom only appears in browser usage. Fix tracked as the new Urgent TODO item (per-app key namespacing + copy-style migration).
  • Further findings documented: all three web/index.html files lack a viewport meta tag (iPhone Safari renders the desktop breakpoint on a ~980 px virtual viewport); web identity is still the Flutter placeholder ("frontend" / "A new Flutter project." in manifest, title, and apple-mobile-web-app-title); service-worker disabling in frontend-pages.yml means web builds cannot launch offline, and Safari ITP can evict all local data after 7 days of inactivity; oauth_callback in backend/notechondria/api_views.py hardcodes the editor path for all same-tab redirect flows.
  • Updated docs/TODO.md: new "Cross-platform web shell" subsection (Urgent storage-namespacing item, viewport meta, web identity, offline/install decision), new "Tutorials" section (course content + seeding, in-app surfacing), OAuth-callback app routing and Casdoor redirect-URI audit items under Backend / Auth, and rewrote the stale Casdoor migration entry — phases 1–3 landed across 0.1.95–0.1.101, only phases 4–5 remain.
  • Linked the new plan doc from docs/SUMMARY.md and docs/readme.md.

Verification

0.1.122 - click-run database and R2 backup scripts

User directive:

in scripts folder of the project root, add python scripts to auto download and backup the database to ./scripts/db_backup/<backup_time>.tar or user selected dir ... and also create the similar version independent scripts for cloudflare storages. add restore scripts for both db and remote storage space. (4 scripts in total)

What changed

Added four standalone Python scripts under repo-root scripts/:

  • scripts/backup_database.py
  • scripts/restore_database.py
  • scripts/backup_cloudflare_r2.py
  • scripts/restore_cloudflare_r2.py

The database scripts read root .env, prefer DATABASE_URL, and fall back to the POSTGRE_* variables. Backups are PostgreSQL tar dumps written to scripts/db_backup/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.tar unless the operator sets USER_SELECTED_BACKUP_DIR.

The database restore script restores the newest tar in the backup directory by default, or the exact RESTORE_FILE set inside the script. It prompts for RESTORE_DATABASE before applying pg_restore.

The Cloudflare R2 scripts read root .env R2 credentials and use Python stdlib SigV4 signing against Cloudflare's S3 API, so they do not need boto3 or AWS CLI. R2 backups are version-independent tar archives written to scripts/r2_backup/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.tar; each archive has a manifest.json plus opaque object payloads under objects/.

The R2 restore script overwrites matching object keys by default and leaves extra remote objects alone. The operator can set DELETE_REMOTE_OBJECTS_NOT_IN_BACKUP = True inside the script for an exact replacement restore.

Docs

Added docs/operations/local_backup_restore.md and linked it from the docs summary and human overview.

0.1.120 — editor signed-out auth widget unified onto shared AuthHub

User directive verbatim:

"continue working on the unified auth hub."

The deferred work from 0.1.119: editor's signed-out account surface was duplicating what the shared AuthHub widget already provided. Portal + planner already used AuthHub (with the same Casdoor SSO pill / signup link / email-password fallback expander); editor hand-rolled its own copy in editor_app/lib/modules/settings_build.dart. This round drops the duplicate and routes editor through the shared widget.

Why the in-line copy existed

When the editor's settings page was first built (0.1.78ish), the AuthHub widget didn't yet exist in notechondria_shared. By the time AuthHub landed, editor had a working surface and nobody went back to consolidate. Maintenance cost showed up over the last several auth-flow rounds: every time the Casdoor primary CTA, signup link, or fallback expander needed a tweak, the change had to be made in two places (editor's _buildSignedOutAccount plus the shared AuthHub), with no compiler help to keep them in sync.

Symptoms across recent versions:

  • 0.1.103: signup wizard removed → had to delete the same code twice.
  • 0.1.108: Casdoor button always-shown → the gate had to be dropped in two places.
  • 0.1.116: "Login via third party" duplicate button removed → again, two edits.

After this round, all three apps render the same AuthHub body. A single edit in notechondria_shared/lib/src/components/ auth_dialogs.dart propagates everywhere.

What changed

frontend/editor_app/lib/modules/settings_build.dart

_buildSignedOutAccount(BuildContext) is now a one-liner:

Widget _buildSignedOutAccount(BuildContext context) {
  return AuthHub(
    apiBaseUrl: widget.apiBaseUrl,
    onLogin: widget.onLogin,
    onCasdoorLogin: widget.onCasdoorLogin,
    casdoorOrgLoginUrl: widget.casdoorOrgLoginUrl,
  );
}

AuthHub is exported by the shared package and already provides:

  • Continue with Casdoor SSO FilledButton (gated on onCasdoorLogin != null),
  • No account? Sign up via Casdoor link (gated on a non-empty casdoorOrgLoginUrl),
  • Use email / password instead expander → EmailPasswordDialog,
  • API-base host subtitle inside the login dialog so the user knows which backend they're authenticating to.

All of those previously had hand-rolled equivalents in editor.

Dead code removed

The following helpers are gone — they were called only by the old _buildSignedOutAccount body:

  • _OAuthPillButton class (the full-width OutlinedButton helper).
  • _legacyAuthBlock (the email/password fallback Column).
  • _openLoginDialog (the EmailPasswordDialog opener).
  • _apiBaseHostSubtitle (the host-derivation helper).
  • _casdoorBrowserLoginUrl getter.
  • _openCasdoorBrowserLogin method.
  • _showLegacyAuthFallback field on _SettingsPageState.
  • toggleLegacyAuthFallback method on _SettingsPageState.

Net: −190 lines from settings_build.dart and a tighter _SettingsPageState interface.

The signed-IN account surface was not unified — that's a settings-navigation menu (Personal information / Sign-in & Security / API settings list rows + logout), not an auth-choice surface, so it has no equivalent in AuthHub. Portal + planner have similar bespoke signed-in cards; unifying those would require a different kind of shared widget and isn't part of this round.

Bark notification rule

Per docs/AGENTS.md, after tests pass and before pushing the operator should send a silent push to every *.bark.env URL. That step was missed when 0.1.117–0.1.119 were pushed; the catchup notification for 0.1.119 was sent inline today before this round started, and 0.1.120's push notification fires after this commit lands.

  1. flutter analyze clean across the four Flutter packages — no new errors, no new warnings. The pre-existing _socialLinkError warning in planner is untouched.
  2. editor_app/lib/modules/settings_build.dart — visually inspected before / after; the SettingsState fields and the _SettingsPageBuildX extension callers all line up.
  3. AuthHub's existing portal + planner surfaces are unchanged (no edits to either app's settings code), so the only risk is regression on the editor's signed-out card. The render is byte-equivalent because AuthHub's body matches the editor's old in-line shape (Casdoor pill + signup link
    • fallback expander, in that order).

In this round, you may read and parse the login info from oidc (avatar, firstname last name, email address, etc realted to creator profile. refresh if they made any changes. Note, never change the username to avoid corruptions). P.S. I noteices that we did not create display name atribute for creator model, add that and show display name by default. it should be optional and we show display names when user configured that in public note author names, etc. otherwise use the default settings.

Remember to add the instructions in the docs for setting up casdoor login providers for custom jwt-token"

Done in five docker-verified stages, all squashed into this one release commit so the rolling deploy picks them up atomically.

Backend

Creator profile fields (migration 0033)

backend/creators/migrations/0033_profile_refresh_drop_social.py makes four schema changes:

  1. Creator.display_name — CharField(max_length=255, blank, default=""). User-facing label preferred over User.username on public surfaces (note bylines, comment headers, sidebar header). Editable from settings (the SPA can PATCH it via the existing /api/v1/settings/ endpoint), but the next Casdoor sign-in re-overwrites with whatever the IdP currently has.
  2. Creator.avatar_url — URLField(max_length=512, blank, default=""). Remote avatar URL refreshed from the JWT's avatar claim on every login. The SPA prefers this over the locally-uploaded Creator.image so a Casdoor profile- pic change propagates everywhere on next login.
  3. Creator.casdoor_profile_synced_at — DateTimeField(blank, null). UTC timestamp of the most recent profile refresh. Drives the 5-minute throttle inside _sync_creator_from_claims.
  4. SocialAccount table dropped along with the SocialProviderChoices enum. Casdoor proxies third-party identities (Google, GitHub, etc.) on its application Providers tab now; the only Notechondria-side link is Creator.casdoor_sub. The legacy migration command (migrate_users_to_casdoor) had its SocialAccount-backed provider pre-population block removed in the same commit so python manage.py migrate_users_to_casdoor ... keeps working on databases where creators_socialaccount is already gone.

_sync_creator_from_claims(creator, claims) helper

New helper in backend/creators/casdoor_auth.py that mirrors the Nextcloud user_oidc plugin's "Sync user attributes on every login" pattern. Updates:

  • Creator.display_name ← <CASDOOR_CLAIM_DISPLAY_NAME>
  • Creator.avatar_url ← <CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR> (new env var, default avatar)
  • User.first_name ← <CASDOOR_CLAIM_GIVEN_NAME>
  • User.last_name ← <CASDOOR_CLAIM_FAMILY_NAME>
  • User.email ← <CASDOOR_CLAIM_EMAIL>

Deliberately not touched:

  • User.username — changing it breaks Django ORM PK references on every owner-keyed FK and every external link to /api/v1/creators/<username>/. Username is set once at account creation (bind or create-with-password path off the 0.1.118 link challenge) and is stable for the lifetime of the account.
  • Creator.image — the locally-uploaded avatar. Left alone so a user who uploaded a custom image inside Notechondria doesn't have it silently replaced by the Casdoor avatar. The SPA prefers avatar_url when set, falls back to image otherwise (resolved server-side in auth_payload).

The helper is throttled to 5-minute granularity via Creator.casdoor_profile_synced_at. Called from:

  • CasdoorJWTAuthentication.authenticate — every JWT- authenticated request (the throttle keeps DB writes manageable on a busy SPA).
  • CasdoorExchangeApiView fast path — when the exchange finds an already-linked account.
  • CasdoorLinkBindApiView and CasdoorLinkCreateApiView — after stamping casdoor_sub. These re-verify the LinkChallenge.access_token to recover the full claims dict, then sync.

Wire-shape additions

auth_payload and SettingsSerializer.to_representation now expose three new fields:

  • display_name — same priority chain everywhere: Creator.display_name → User.first_name + last_name → User.username.
  • avatar_url — Creator.avatar_url (or empty).
  • image_url — kept for backward compat; Creator.avatar_url preferred over the local Creator.image URL.
  • casdoor_profile_synced_at — ISO-8601 timestamp.

SettingsSerializer.update accepts a writable display_name field; the change persists locally until the next Casdoor login overwrites it.

CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR env var

backend/notechondria/settings.py reads CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR=os.getenv("CASDOOR_CLAIM_AVATAR", "avatar"). Operators with a Casdoor instance that names the avatar field differently can override (comma-separated list, first non-empty wins — same pattern as the other CASDOOR_CLAIM_* vars from 0.1.110).

Frontend

"Manage Casdoor account" button + admin-contact help text

Added to all three apps' Connected Accounts UIs:

  • editor: _ConnectedAccountsSection in editor_app/lib/modules/settings_sections.dart — gained a casdoorOrgLoginUrl parameter, renders an OutlinedButton ("Manage Casdoor account") that navigates the browser to the org-themed login page when the URL is non-empty. Plus the text: "If sign-in is unavailable, contact your Notechondria admin (Casdoor backend may be off)." Threaded from _SignInSecurityPage.
  • portal: same in portal_app/lib/modules/settings.dart, threaded from _ConnectedAccountsPage in settings_pages.dart.
  • planner: same in planner_app/lib/modules/settings.dart, threaded inline from the account card.

The URL itself is never hardcoded: it comes from /api/v1/auth/casdoor/config/'s signin_url field, which the backend builds from ${CASDOOR_ENDPOINT}/login/${CASDOOR_ORG_NAME}. For the user's current Northflank env, that resolves to https://auth.trance-0.com/login/trance-0.

Settings menu consistency — Agent Skill placement

Per the user's complaint that Agent Skill (MCP skill markdown) appears in different sections per app:

  • editor: unchanged — Agent Skill already lived on _ApiSettingsPage next to the MCP API key + GitHub Sync card. This is the canonical pattern.
  • portal: moved off _SignInSecurityPage and onto _ApiSettingsPage so it sits next to the MCP API key controls. Sign-in & Security now shows a one-line pointer to the Account page for Casdoor bind/unlink.
  • planner: planner has only one settings page (no subpages yet), so Agent Skill moved out of the inline account card and into a sibling Card alongside the GitHub Sync card. A TODO marker notes the future split into subpages to match the editor + portal pattern.

Deferred work

The user also asked for a deeper unification: "I don't see the reason for using different login widget for the three apps." Editor uses its own _buildSignedInAccount / _buildSignedOutAccount helpers in editor_app/lib/modules/settings_build.dart; portal + planner share the AuthHub widget from notechondria_shared/lib/src/ components/auth_dialogs.dart.

Refactoring editor onto AuthHub is a deeper change with more surface area (different parent state contracts, different controllers). Deferred to a separate round so this commit stays focused on data + UX-thread changes the operator can deploy together.

0.1.118 — gitea-style Casdoor link-challenge flow (bind existing or create new with chosen password)

User directive verbatim:

"Yes, I believe that one is safer for migrating accounts and better than the nextcloud flows. I don't see any additional variables need to configured with that so continue please."

(Confirming the proposal from 0.1.117's deferred-work section.)

The 0.1.96-era Casdoor exchange auto-linked-by-email and auto-provisioned-by-sub. Both were silent identity decisions — a brand-new Casdoor identity with no email match would silently create a fresh account with set_unusable_password(), leaving the user with no idea which Notechondria account they had landed on or whether their pre-existing legacy account had been adopted. For a migration where users own multiple Notechondria accounts (some on the legacy hasher, some not yet linked), the silent path is too easy to get wrong.

This round replaces both implicit branches with an explicit two-choice dialog modeled on Gitea's account-linking flow.

Flow

┌─ SPA: redirect to Casdoor → user signs in
│
├─ SPA: POST /auth/casdoor/exchange/   {code}
│  └─ Backend: verify JWT, run group ACL, look up casdoor_sub
│     ├─ existing link → return auth_payload   (fast path; same as before)
│     └─ no link       → create LinkChallenge, return:
│        {link_challenge, expires_at, casdoor_identity, suggested_username}
│
├─ SPA: detects `link_challenge` → show CasdoorLinkChallengeDialog
│  ├─ User picks "Bind existing":
│  │  └─ POST /auth/casdoor/link/bind/   {nonce, username, password}
│  │     └─ Backend: legacy-auth check, stamp casdoor_sub, return auth_payload
│  └─ User picks "Create new":
│     └─ POST /auth/casdoor/link/create/   {nonce, password}
│        └─ Backend: create User w/ password, stamp casdoor_sub, seed Inbox,
│                    return auth_payload
│
└─ SPA: applyAuthPayload as usual

The Casdoor JWT sits server-side on the LinkChallenge row keyed by a 48-char URL-safe nonce; the SPA never sees it before the link decision and never has to round-trip back to Casdoor for a fresh code (Casdoor codes are one-time use). Challenge expires in 10 minutes.

Backend — what's new

backend/creators/models.py

New LinkChallenge model:

FieldNotes
nonce48-char URL-safe random; unique, indexed
subCasdoor user sub claim — what we stamp onto Creator.casdoor_sub
casdoor_username, casdoor_email, casdoor_display_name, casdoor_groupscaptured from the verified JWT
access_tokenthe verified JWT, replayed back in auth_payload after the link completes
created_at, expires_at (10 min)one-time-use ticket; is_expired() helper
Meta.indexes(sub, expires_at) for cheap garbage-collection sweeps

backend/creators/migrations/0032_link_challenge.py — auto- generated by manage.py makemigrations inside the docker build container; verified clean by manage.py check.

backend/creators/casdoor_auth.py

_resolve_user (the auto-link-by-email + auto-provision-by-sub implementation) is gone. The fast-path-only replacement is _resolve_existing_user: returns the matching User when Creator.casdoor_sub == claims['sub'], otherwise None so the caller can mint a LinkChallenge.

_resolve_user is kept as a backwards-compat alias so older callers (e.g. test files imported from outside the Casdoor flow) still resolve.

backend/creators/api.py

CasdoorExchangeApiView:

  • Now imports _resolve_existing_user, _check_group_access, _claim_groups, _claim_str directly so the exchange logic is readable end-to-end.
  • Group ACL gate moved here from CasdoorJWTAuthentication. authenticate — it now applies to both the exchange path and the JWT-bearer path, closing a gap where a user who passed the ACL once at exchange time could keep using the same JWT after being removed from the group. (Group check at authenticate-time still runs, this is additive.)
  • After verifying the JWT and finding no existing link, mints a LinkChallenge with a 48-char nonce and 10-minute TTL, garbage-collects expired rows for the same sub, returns a response with shape: 
    {
  "link_challenge": "<nonce>",
  "expires_at": "<iso8601>",
  "casdoor_identity": {"username", "email", "display_name"},
  "suggested_username": "<username or email-localpart>"
}

Two new views:

  • CasdoorLinkBindApiView (POST /auth/casdoor/link/bind/): Accepts {nonce, username|email|identifier, password}. Looks up the legacy user case-insensitively (email first, then username), authenticates via django.contrib.auth. authenticate(), stamps Creator.casdoor_sub = challenge.sub, deletes the challenge, returns the standard auth_payload with the captured Casdoor JWT as the token.
  • CasdoorLinkCreateApiView (POST /auth/casdoor/link/create/): Accepts {nonce, password}. Refuses (409) when a legacy account already exists for the Casdoor email — the SPA should redirect to bind. Otherwise creates a fresh User + Creator using username/email/display-name from the captured JWT claims, sets the user-chosen password, stamps casdoor_sub, runs seed_inbox_and_welcome_note, returns the standard auth_payload.

Both completion endpoints delete the LinkChallenge row on success or on 409-conflict resolution; expired challenges are silently swept.

backend/notechondria/api_urls.py

Two new routes wired immediately after casdoor/exchange/:

auth/casdoor/link/bind/      → CasdoorLinkBindApiView
auth/casdoor/link/create/    → CasdoorLinkCreateApiView

Frontend — what's new

notechondria_shared

  • lib/src/app_shell/auth_client.dart: declared the two new abstract methods on AuthClient — casdoorLinkBind({nonce, identifier, password}) and casdoorLinkCreate({nonce, password}). Each returns the standard auth_payload.
  • lib/src/components/casdoor_link_challenge_dialog.dart (new): the gitea-style choice + form dialog. Three stages: choose (two pill-buttons), bind (legacy username/email + password), create (new password + confirm with ≥8 char enforcement). Returns a CasdoorLinkChallengeDecision via Navigator.pop. The dialog never carries the Casdoor JWT — only the nonce travels through the form, so a cancelled / closed dialog leaves no client-side credential trail.
  • lib/notechondria_shared.dart: exported the dialog + decision class.
  • lib/src/app_shell/app_shell_oauth_mixin.dart:
    • handleOAuthCallback now branches on the exchange response: link_challenge non-empty → call onCasdoorLinkChallenge(payload) and return its result; otherwise the existing applyAuthPayload fast path runs.
    • New default-implementation onCasdoorLinkChallenge method on the mixin: pops the dialog, dispatches the chosen completion endpoint, threads the resulting auth_payload through applyAuthPayload. Apps can override on _AppShellState for a custom UX, but the default is enough for editor / planner / portal — they all want the same dialog. Logs each transition under source <App>.Auth/casdoor.link_challenge so the user can grep the debug log for the bind/create decision and completion outcome.

Per-app

  • frontend/editor_app/lib/core/http_client.dart, frontend/portal_app/lib/core/client.dart, frontend/planner_app/lib/core/client.dart: concrete casdoorLinkBind / casdoorLinkCreate implementations. Each app's NotechondriaClient already extends AuthClient, so the new methods are inherited as abstract and need a concrete impl per app — done.

Behavior matrix

Casdoor identity stateExchange returnsSPA shows
Linked (existing casdoor_sub)auth_payloadnothing extra; signed in immediately
Not linked, fresh JWTlink_challenge payloadbind/create dialog
Group ACL fails403 with consequence/causesnackbar from existing error path
expires_at passed before completionbind/create endpoints 400snackbar; user restarts SSO

Group-ACL-rejected users never reach the dialog — the exchange endpoint 403s before LinkChallenge creation, so no orphan rows build up.

In-container Django bootstrap smoke test — confirmed creators.api.CasdoorLinkBindApiView, CasdoorLinkCreateApiView, and creators.models.LinkChallenge import without error and the LinkChallenge model carries every expected field (nonce, sub, casdoor_username, casdoor_email, casdoor_display_name, casdoor_groups, access_token, created_at, expires_at).
